observed: All verified federal funding, $2,474,731, sits on a single DOE contract line (DE-SC0020921) whose period of performance ended 2025-11-15.
inferred: Attacks BOTH gating constraints on persistent ocean sensing at once - power and biofouling - which is unusual. Most companies address one and inherit the other.
The retrofit framing (a module for existing sensors) is commercially smarter than a new sensor platform: it sells into an installed base rather than displacing it.

Publicly reported output of 0.91 W average against an expected 7-8 W time-averaged annual yield is roughly an order of magnitude below target. This may reflect deployment conditions or an unresolved conversion problem; the gap is the central technical question.

Queue 'tier_a'. For: Technical evidence 3/3: built, demonstrated, patented or Phase I+. Commercialization evidence 2/3. Propeller relevance 3/3 with ocean centrality 'central_mechanism'. Current activity: latest signal 2025-12-04 (~9 months old). Against: none

PHASE 2.5 CORRECTION. Phase 2 characterised the 0.91 W result as roughly an order-of-magnitude shortfall against a 7-8 W target. OOI frames it as achieved 'even in relatively low-energy conditions', so it is a single measurement in benign sea states and is not directly comparable to an annual time-average. The honest statement is that reconciling the two is an open technical question, not that the technology underperformed.
unknown: No public evidence of a paying customer, unit price, or manufacturing plan. OOI is a co-development partner, not necessarily a purchaser.

No public evidence of federal funding beyond Nov 2025, of equity financing at any point, or of a paying customer. OOI is a co-development partner, not necessarily a purchaser.

Whether the company is actively commercializing in 2026 cannot be established from public sources. The website is live with a 2025 copyright and the most recent third-party coverage is Dec 2025. Absence of evidence is not evidence of failure, but it is also not evidence of momentum.
what_must_be_true: A wave energy converter small enough to sit on a buoy must deliver enough average power, reliably enough, to beat simply oversizing the battery and servicing it on the existing ship schedule.
technical_kill_question: Is the 0.91 W measured output a site/sea-state artefact or a fundamental limit of the rack-and-pinion tilt conversion? If the latter, the UV duty cycle needed to prevent fouling may never be sustainable on harvested power alone.
commercial_kill_question: Ocean observing budgets are largely federal and grant-funded. If the buyer is only NSF/NOAA programme budgets, this is a small, slow market regardless of how well the technology works - and current federal funding uncertainty is acknowledged by the CEO.
